intended_object: For an element x of the restricted product Πʳ (R i, A i) with respect to the cofinite filter, this is the finite set of indices where x is exceptional, S(x) = {i | x i ∉ A i}. In the adelic setting it is the finite set of places where x is not integral. Inferred from the docstring, the name and its use in `mem_cofiniteStage_exceptionalFinset`.
explanation:
An element x of a cofinite restricted product carries a proof `x.2` that x i ∈ A i holds for all but finitely many i. `Filter.eventually_cofinite` turns this into finiteness of the set {i | ¬ x i ∈ A i}, and `Set.Finite.toFinset` converts that set into a `Finset`. So the definition gives exactly the set of exceptional coordinates, with no extra or missing conditions.

The degenerate cases come out right. If x lies in Π A i, the set is empty. If ι is finite, it is still the set of coordinates where x i ∉ A i.

The generality is natural: the index type, the factors and the subsets are all arbitrary. The construction only makes sense for the cofinite filter, because finiteness of the exceptional set is exactly what that filter provides, so restricting to it is not too narrow.

I found no Mathlib declaration that names this finset. Mathlib only states the property `x.2` as an eventually-statement. The library uses the definition as the canonical finite set S with x ∈ Π_{i∈S} R i × Π_{i∉S} A i, which matches its standard meaning.
